passages.text: “If you will return, O Israel, return to Me,” declares the LORD. “If you will remove your detestable idols from My sight and no longer waver, and if you can swear, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then the nations will be blessed by Him, and in Him they will glory.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
The LORD says, “If you return, Israel, return to Me.
Remove your detestable idols from My presence.
Do not waver.
Swear, ‘As surely as the LORD lives.’
Speak in truth.
Speak in justice.
Speak in righteousness.
Then the nations will be blessed by the LORD.
The nations will glory in the LORD.”
passages.original: אִם־ תָּשׁ֨וּב יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל׀ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י תָּשׁ֑וּב וְאִם־ תָּסִ֧יר שִׁקּוּצֶ֛יךָ מִפָּנַ֖י וְלֹ֥א תָנֽוּד׃ וְנִשְׁבַּ֙עְתָּ֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט וּבִצְדָקָ֑ה וְהִתְבָּ֥רְכוּ ב֛וֹ גּוֹיִ֖ם וּב֥וֹ יִתְהַלָּֽלוּ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: “Break up your unplowed ground, and do not sow among the thorns.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the men of Judah and Jerusalem.
He gives a command.
He says, “Break up your unplowed ground.
Do not sow seed among thorns.”
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהֹוָ֗ה לְאִ֤ישׁ יְהוּדָה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם נִ֥ירוּ לָכֶ֖ם נִ֑יר וְאַֽל־ תִּזְרְע֖וּ אֶל־ קוֹצִֽים׃

passages.text: Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts, O men of Judah and people of Jerusalem. Otherwise, My wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem.
He commands them to circumcise themselves to Him.
He tells them to remove the hardness from their hearts.
He warns them to do this because of their evil deeds.
If they do not obey, His anger will come out like fire.
His wrath will burn, and no one will be able to put it out.
passages.original: הִמֹּ֣לוּ לַיהֹוָ֗ה וְהָסִ֙רוּ֙ עָרְל֣וֹת לְבַבְכֶ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה וְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם פֶּן־ תֵּצֵ֨א כָאֵ֜שׁ חֲמָתִ֗י וּבָעֲרָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין מְכַבֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י רֹ֥עַ מַעַלְלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say: “Blow the ram’s horn throughout the land. Cry aloud and say, ‘Assemble yourselves and let us flee to the fortified cities.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
He commands them to make an announcement in Judah.
He tells them to proclaim this message in Jerusalem.
He instructs them to blow the ram’s horn throughout the land.
He tells them to cry aloud.
He commands them to say, “Assemble yourselves.”
He tells them to say, “Let us flee to the fortified cities.”
passages.original: הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ וְאִמְר֕וּ וְתִקְעוּ שׁוֹפָ֖ר בָּאָ֑רֶץ קִרְא֤וּ מַלְאוּ֙ וְאִמְר֔וּ הֵאָסְפ֥וּ וְנָב֖וֹאָה אֶל־ עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָֽר׃

passages.text: Raise a signal flag toward Zion. Seek refuge! Do not delay! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and terrible destruction.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God commands them to act quickly.
Raise a signal flag toward Zion.
Seek safety in Zion.
Do not wait.
Do not stand still.
God is bringing disaster from the north.
God is sending terrible destruction.
passages.original: שְׂאוּ־ נֵ֣ס צִיּ֔וֹנָה הָעִ֖יזוּ אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹ֑דוּ כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his lair to lay waste your land. Your cities will be reduced to ruins and lie uninhabited.
passages.sermon:
A lion has left his thicket.
A destroyer of nations has set out.
He has left his home.
He will make your land a wasteland.
Your cities will become ruins.
No one will live in them.
passages.original: עָלָ֤ה אַרְיֵה֙ מִֽסֻּבְּכ֔וֹ וּמַשְׁחִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם נָסַ֖ע יָצָ֣א מִמְּקֹמ֑וֹ לָשׂ֤וּם אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ תִּצֶּ֖ינָה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: So put on sackcloth, mourn and wail, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is angry with us.
His fierce anger has not turned away.
Put on sackcloth.
Mourn.
Wail.
passages.original: עַל־ זֹ֛את חִגְר֥וּ שַׂקִּ֖ים סִפְד֣וּ וְהֵילִ֑ילוּ כִּ֥י לֹא־ שָׁ֛ב חֲר֥וֹן אַף־ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃פ

passages.text: “In that day,” declares the LORD, “the king and officials will lose their courage. The priests will tremble in fear, and the prophets will be astounded.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about a coming day.
On that day, the king will lose his courage.
The officials will also lose their courage.
The priests will tremble with fear.
The prophets will stand in shock.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה בַיּוֹם־ הַהוּא֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה יֹאבַ֥ד לֵב־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְלֵ֣ב הַשָּׂרִ֑ים וְנָשַׁ֙מּוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וְהַנְּבִיאִ֖ים יִתְמָֽהוּ׃

passages.text: Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD, how completely You have deceived this people and Jerusalem by saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while a sword is at our throats.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah spoke to God.
Jeremiah said, "Ah, Lord GOD."
Jeremiah accused God of deceiving the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
God told the people, "You will have peace."
But danger came instead.
A sword now threatens our lives.
passages.original: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אָכֵן֩ הַשֵּׁ֨א הִשֵּׁ֜אתָ לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁל֖וֹם יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְנָגְעָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב עַד־ הַנָּֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem, “A searing wind from the barren heights in the desert blows toward the daughter of My people, but not to winnow or to sift; a wind too strong for that comes from Me. Now I also pronounce judgments against them.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people and to Jerusalem.
He says this at a certain time.
A hot, dry wind comes from the desert hills.
This wind blows toward the people God calls His daughter.
This wind does not come to separate grain or to clean it.
This wind is too strong for that purpose.
God sends this wind Himself.
God now announces His judgments against the people.
passages.original: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יֵאָמֵ֤ר לָֽעָם־ הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם ר֣וּחַ צַ֤ח שְׁפָיִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר דֶּ֖רֶךְ בַּת־ עַמִּ֑י ל֥וֹא לִזְר֖וֹת וְל֥וֹא לְהָבַֽר׃ ר֧וּחַ מָלֵ֛א מֵאֵ֖לֶּה יָ֣בוֹא לִ֑י עַתָּ֕ה גַּם־ אֲנִ֛י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר מִשְׁפָּטִ֖ים אוֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, he advances like the clouds, his chariots like the whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
passages.sermon:
An enemy comes.
He moves forward like clouds in the sky.
His chariots rush like a whirlwind.
His horses run faster than eagles.
We are in great trouble.
We are destroyed.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֣ה׀ כַּעֲנָנִ֣ים יַעֲלֶ֗ה וְכַסּוּפָה֙ מַרְכְּבוֹתָ֔יו קַלּ֥וּ מִנְּשָׁרִ֖ים סוּסָ֑יו א֥וֹי לָ֖נוּ כִּ֥י שֻׁדָּֽדְנוּ׃

passages.text: Wash the evil from your heart, O Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will you harbor wicked thoughts within you?
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem, you have evil in your heart.
Remove this evil from your heart.
If you do this, you will be saved.
You keep wicked thoughts inside you.
How long will you keep these wicked thoughts?
passages.original: כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לְמַ֖עַן תִּוָּשֵׁ֑עִי עַד־ מָתַ֛י תָּלִ֥ין בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ךְ מַחְשְׁב֥וֹת אוֹנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: For a voice resounds from Dan, proclaiming disaster from the hills of Ephraim.
passages.sermon:
A voice comes from Dan.
This voice announces news.
The news is about disaster.
The sound of disaster comes from the hills of Ephraim.
passages.original: כִּ֛י ק֥וֹל מַגִּ֖יד מִדָּ֑ן וּמַשְׁמִ֥יעַ אָ֖וֶן מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Warn the nations now! Proclaim to Jerusalem: “A besieging army comes from a distant land; they raise their voices against the cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Jeremiah speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He tells them to warn the nations.
He says, “Look! Announce this to Jerusalem.
A besieging army comes from a distant land.
This army raises its voice against the cities of Judah.”
passages.original: הַזְכִּ֣ירוּ לַגּוֹיִ֗ם הִנֵּה֙ הַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם נֹצְרִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים מֵאֶ֣רֶץ הַמֶּרְחָ֑ק וַֽיִּתְּנ֛וּ עַל־ עָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה קוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: They surround her like men guarding a field, because she has rebelled against Me,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says Jerusalem has rebelled against Him.
Enemies surround Jerusalem on every side.
They act like men who guard a field.
passages.original: כְּשֹׁמְרֵ֣י שָׂדַ֔י הָי֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ מִסָּבִ֑יב כִּי־ אֹתִ֥י מָרָ֖תָה נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “Your ways and deeds have brought this upon you. This is your punishment; how bitter it is, because it pierces to the heart!”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jerusalem and Judah.
God says, “Your actions have caused this trouble.
Your choices and your deeds brought this punishment.
This suffering is your own doing.
This punishment is very bitter.
This pain reaches deep into your heart.”
passages.original: דַּרְכֵּךְ֙ וּמַ֣עֲלָלַ֔יִךְ עָשׂ֥וֹ אֵ֖לֶּה לָ֑ךְ זֹ֤את רָעָתֵךְ֙ כִּ֣י מָ֔ר כִּ֥י נָגַ֖ע עַד־ לִבֵּֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! Oh, the pain in my chest! My heart pounds within me; I cannot be silent. For I have heard the sound of the horn, the alarm of battle.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks.
He feels deep anguish.
He cries out, “My anguish! My anguish!”
He writhes in pain.
He feels pain in his chest.
His heart pounds inside him.
He cannot keep silent.
He has heard the sound of the horn.
He has heard the alarm of battle.
passages.original: מֵעַ֣י׀ מֵעַ֨י׀ אָחוּלָה קִיר֥וֹת לִבִּ֛י הֹֽמֶה־ לִּ֥י לִבִּ֖י לֹ֣א אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י ק֤וֹל שׁוֹפָר֙ שָׁמַעְתִּי נַפְשִׁ֔י תְּרוּעַ֖ת מִלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Disaster after disaster is proclaimed, for the whole land is laid waste. My tents are destroyed in an instant, my curtains in a moment.
passages.sermon:
God speaks through the prophet Jeremiah.
God announces disaster after disaster.
The whole land is laid waste.
My tents are destroyed in an instant.
My curtains are ruined in a moment.
passages.original: שֶׁ֤בֶר עַל־ שֶׁ֙בֶר֙ נִקְרָ֔א כִּ֥י שֻׁדְּדָ֖ה כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ פִּתְאֹם֙ שֻׁדְּד֣וּ אֹהָלַ֔י רֶ֖גַע יְרִיעֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the horn?
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks.
He feels deep anguish.
He sees disaster coming to his people.
He asks a question.
He says, "How long must I see the signal flag?"
He says, "How long must I hear the sound of the horn?"
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַ֖י אֶרְאֶה־ נֵּ֑ס אֶשְׁמְעָ֖ה ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃ס

passages.text: “For My people are fools; they have not known Me. They are foolish children, without understanding. They are skilled in doing evil, but they know not how to do good.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people.
God says, "My people are fools."
They do not know Me.
They are foolish children.
They do not understand.
They know how to do evil.
They do not know how to do good.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ אֱוִ֣יל עַמִּ֗י אוֹתִי֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ בָּנִ֤ים סְכָלִים֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְלֹ֥א נְבוֹנִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה חֲכָמִ֥ים הֵ֙מָּה֙ לְהָרַ֔ע וּלְהֵיטִ֖יב לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah looked at the earth.
He saw the earth.
The earth was formless.
The earth was empty.
Jeremiah looked to the heavens.
The heavens had no light.
passages.original: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְהִנֵּה־ תֹ֖הוּ וָבֹ֑הוּ וְאֶל־ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֵ֥ין אוֹרָֽם׃

passages.text: I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah saw a vision from God.
He looked at the mountains.
The mountains were shaking.
He saw all the hills.
The hills were moving back and forth.
passages.original: רָאִ֙יתִי֙ הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וְהִנֵּ֖ה רֹעֲשִׁ֑ים וְכָל־ הַגְּבָע֖וֹת הִתְקַלְקָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: I looked, and no man was left; all the birds of the air had fled.
passages.sermon: The prophet Jeremiah looked at the earth.\r\nHe saw that no person remained.\r\nHe saw that all the birds of the sky had flown away.
passages.original: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֖ה אֵ֣ין הָאָדָ֑ם וְכָל־ ע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נָדָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: I looked, and the fruitful land was a desert. All its cities were torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah saw a vision from God.
He looked at the land.
The fruitful land had become a desert.
All the cities in the land were destroyed.
The LORD did this.
The LORD acted in fierce anger.
passages.original: רָאִ֕יתִי וְהִנֵּ֥ה הַכַּרְמֶ֖ל הַמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְכָל־ עָרָ֗יו נִתְּצוּ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י חֲר֥וֹן אַפּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says: “The whole land will be desolate, but I will not finish its destruction.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD has great power and authority.
The LORD says this message.
The whole land will become desolate.
I, the LORD, will not destroy everything completely.
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שְׁמָמָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכָלָ֖ה לֹ֥א אֶעֱשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: Therefore the earth will mourn and the heavens above will grow dark. I have spoken, I have planned, and I will not relent or turn back.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority and power.
God says, “The earth will mourn.
The heavens above will grow dark.
I have spoken these words.
I have made this plan.
I will not change my mind.
I will not turn back from what I have decided.”
passages.original: עַל־ זֹאת֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְקָדְר֥וּ הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם מִמָּ֑עַל עַ֤ל כִּי־ דִבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ זַמֹּ֔תִי וְלֹ֥א נִחַ֖מְתִּי וְלֹא־ אָשׁ֥וּב מִמֶּֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Every city flees at the sound of the horseman and archer. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no inhabitant is left.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of the land.
The people hear the sound of the horseman.
They also hear the sound of the archer.
Every city flees because of this sound.
The people run into the thickets.
They climb up among the rocks.
Every city becomes abandoned.
No person remains in them.
passages.original: מִקּ֨וֹל פָּרָ֜שׁ וְרֹ֣מֵה קֶ֗שֶׁת בֹּרַ֙חַת֙ כָּל־ הָעִ֔יר בָּ֚אוּ בֶּעָבִ֔ים וּבַכֵּפִ֖ים עָל֑וּ כָּל־ הָעִ֣יר עֲזוּבָ֔ה וְאֵין־ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּהֵ֖ן אִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: And you, O devastated one, what will you do, though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold jewelry, though you enlarge your eyes with paint? You adorn yourself in vain; your lovers despise you; they want to take your life.
passages.sermon:
You are devastated.
What will you do?
You dress yourself in scarlet.
You put on gold jewelry.
You paint your eyes to make them look larger.
You try to make yourself beautiful.
You do this in vain.
Your lovers despise you.
They want to take your life.
passages.original: וְאַתִּי שָׁד֜וּד מַֽה־ תַּעֲשִׂ֗י כִּֽי־ תִלְבְּשִׁ֨י שָׁנִ֜י כִּי־ תַעְדִּ֣י עֲדִי־ זָהָ֗ב כִּֽי־ תִקְרְעִ֤י בַפּוּךְ֙ עֵינַ֔יִךְ לַשָּׁ֖וְא תִּתְיַפִּ֑י מָאֲסוּ־ בָ֥ךְ עֹגְבִ֖ים נַפְשֵׁ֥ךְ יְבַקֵּֽשׁוּ׃

passages.text: For I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a cry of anguish like one bearing her first child— the cry of the Daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands to say, “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks about Jerusalem.
He hears a cry.
The cry sounds like a woman in labor.
It is a cry of pain.
It is like the pain of a woman giving birth to her first child.
The Daughter of Zion cries out.
She gasps for breath.
She stretches out her hands.
She says, “Woe is me.”
She says, “My soul is faint.”
She says, “Murderers are near.”
passages.original: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי צָרָה֙ כְּמַבְכִּירָ֔ה ק֧וֹל בַּת־ צִיּ֛וֹן תִּתְיַפֵּ֖חַ תְּפָרֵ֣שׂ כַּפֶּ֑יהָ אֽוֹי־ נָ֣א לִ֔י כִּֽי־ עָיְפָ֥ה נַפְשִׁ֖י לְהֹרְגִֽים׃פ
